title: US Inflation Shock: October CPI Hits 0.4% — Is Another Fed Rate Hike About to Shake Crypto Markets?
subTitle:
Wall Street is watching inflation. Crypto investors should be watching where the money goes next. A single Fed decision could change the outlook for BNB, ETH and PEPE.
The latest US inflation report has given financial markets another reason to stay cautious.
Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above economists' expectations of 0.3%. That was slower than September's 0.6% increase, but inflation remains stubborn.
The timing matters. Before the report, CME FedWatch showed a 98.9% probability of a 25-basis-point Fed rate increase in December.
For crypto investors, the bigger question is what happens to global liquidity if the Federal Reserve keeps monetary policy tight.
This is where inflation, geopolitics and institutional capital flows meet.
1. October CPI: A Small Improvement, But Not Enough
The slowdown from 0.6% to 0.4% is encouraging. However, it does not mean the inflation problem is over.
The Federal Reserve needs consistent evidence that price pressures are easing before it can comfortably consider lowering interest rates.
There is also a data limitation. The October year-over-year CPI figure is unavailable because of the disruption associated with the 2025 US government shutdown.
That makes it harder to compare the latest reading with the usual annual inflation benchmark.
The key takeaway: Inflation is showing some moderation, but the latest report gives the Fed little reason to rush towards monetary easing.
2. Why Geopolitics Matters More Than Many Crypto Investors Realize
Inflation is not driven by consumer demand alone.
Wars, tariffs, trade restrictions and shipping disruptions can push production and transportation costs higher.
Take energy markets as an example. If geopolitical tensions threaten important oil supply routes, energy prices can rise. Businesses then face higher operating costs, some of which eventually reach consumers.
That creates another challenge for the Federal Reserve.
The market transmission looks like this:
Geopolitical tensions → Higher energy and shipping costs → Persistent inflation → Restrictive Fed policy → Stronger dollar → Tighter global liquidity → Pressure on crypto.
The US has considerable influence over global financial conditions because the dollar remains central to international trade and finance.
When US interest rates rise, dollar-denominated investments become more attractive. Some institutional capital may move away from emerging markets and speculative assets.
That is how political decisions and monetary policy in Washington can affect a crypto investor's portfolio, even thousands of miles away.
3. The Historical Lesson: Liquidity Changes Everything
The relationship between interest rates and financial markets has been demonstrated repeatedly.
During Paul Volcker's inflation-fighting campaign in the late 1970s and early 1980s, aggressive monetary tightening reshaped the global economic environment.
In 2022, the Federal Reserve's rapid rate increases put pressure on technology stocks, venture capital and cryptocurrencies.
The underlying lesson remains relevant:
When borrowing becomes more expensive, investors become more selective about risk.
Crypto is particularly sensitive to liquidity conditions because market valuations often depend on investor confidence, leverage and expectations of future growth.
However, higher interest rates do not automatically make every cryptocurrency a losing investment.
Projects with meaningful adoption and sustainable network activity can have a different investment profile from purely speculative tokens.
This distinction is important when evaluating BNB, ETH and PEPE.
4. The December Fed Decision: Where Will Institutional Capital Move?
Before the October CPI release, CME FedWatch showed a 98.9% probability of a 25-basis-point rate increase in December.
The hotter-than-expected inflation reading strengthens the case for continued monetary caution.
Institutional investors are not waiting for the actual announcement. They are already assessing Treasury yields, dollar strength, interest-rate derivatives and global liquidity.
Three indicators deserve attention:
Treasury yields: Higher yields make government securities more competitive against volatile investments.
US dollar: Dollar strength can tighten financial conditions for emerging markets and international borrowers.
Institutional positioning: When uncertainty rises, fund managers may reduce speculative exposure and increase defensive allocations.
The Federal Reserve faces a difficult balancing act: controlling inflation without unnecessarily damaging employment and economic growth.
For crypto investors, the important question is not simply whether the Fed raises rates by 25 basis points.
It is whether policymakers signal that restrictive monetary policy will continue beyond December.
5. BNB, ETH and PEPE: Three Different Investment Narratives
The CPI report will not affect every cryptocurrency equally. Each asset has different strengths, risks and sources of demand.
BNB: Ecosystem Utility Could Be Its Advantage
BNB's investment case is closely connected to the BNB Chain ecosystem, transaction activity, network fees and token utility.
That gives it a different market narrative from purely sentiment-driven tokens.
If broader crypto liquidity weakens, BNB can still face selling pressure. But sustained ecosystem activity may help support its longer-term investment case.
Bullish catalysts:
Growing BNB Chain activity.
Expansion of ecosystem applications.
Higher transaction demand.
Recovery in broader crypto liquidity.
Key risks:
Stronger dollar and higher interest rates.
Declining trading activity.
Regulatory and ecosystem-related uncertainty.
What to watch: Network activity, transaction volume, token supply dynamics and ecosystem growth.
ETH: Institutional Adoption and Financial Infrastructure
Ethereum's investment case extends beyond short-term price speculation.
It remains an important network for decentralized finance, stablecoins, tokenization and smart-contract applications.
Growing institutional participation and demand for blockchain-based financial infrastructure could support its longer-term relevance.
But higher Treasury yields can make investors more selective about allocating capital to crypto.
Bullish catalysts:
Stronger institutional participation.
Growth in stablecoin and tokenization activity.
Improving spot ETH ETF flows.
Increasing demand for Ethereum-based applications.
Key risks:
Persistent ETF outflows.
Higher Treasury yields.
Weak network economics.
Reduced speculative demand.
What to watch: ETF flows, staking participation, network fees, stablecoin activity and ETH/BTC strength.
PEPE: High Potential Volatility, High Speculative Risk
PEPE offers a very different investment proposition.
Its valuation is heavily influenced by community sentiment, trading activity, speculative liquidity and broader meme-coin demand.
When market liquidity improves, meme coins can attract significant attention. But when monetary conditions tighten, they can also experience sharp declines.
Bullish catalysts:
Renewed meme-coin interest.
Increasing spot trading volume.
Stronger altcoin sentiment.
Improved speculative liquidity.
Key risks:
Leveraged liquidations.
Declining trading volume.
Whale concentration.
Weakening market sentiment.
What to watch: Spot volume, futures open interest, funding rates, liquidation levels and large-wallet activity.
Comparing the Three Assets
Asset	Main investment narrative	Relative risk
BNB	Ecosystem utility	High
ETH	Institutional infrastructure	High
PEPE	Speculative liquidity	Very high
BNB and ETH have identifiable ecosystem and infrastructure demand. PEPE depends much more heavily on market sentiment and speculative capital.
Investors should not treat these three assets as interchangeable opportunities.
6. From Washington to Your Portfolio: How the Money Moves
For ordinary investors, understanding how political and economic decisions affect capital flows is more useful than reacting to every headline.
Consider these scenarios:
Global development	Market reaction	Potential portfolio impact
US tariff escalation	Higher import costs	Inflation uncertainty
Energy supply disruption	Rising oil prices	Pressure on risk assets
Fed rate increase	Higher cost of capital	Reduced speculative appetite
Stronger US dollar	Tighter global liquidity	Pressure on altcoins
Monetary easing	Potential liquidity improvement	Better risk appetite
Institutional crypto inflows	Increased market demand	Potential support for BNB and ETH
One important detail: financial markets are forward-looking.
If investors have already priced in a December rate increase, the actual announcement may not trigger another major sell-off.
What matters is the Fed's guidance about future policy.
A 25-basis-point increase accompanied by a possible pause could produce a very different reaction from the same increase accompanied by warnings of further tightening.
7. Three Scenarios Crypto Investors Should Prepare For
Scenario A — Bullish: Inflation Starts Cooling
If inflation moderates and the Fed signals a pause, Treasury yields and the dollar could lose momentum.
Institutional risk appetite may improve.
BNB and ETH could attract renewed capital.
PEPE could benefit from a broader speculative altcoin rally.
However, PEPE would remain the riskiest exposure.
Scenario B — Base Case: The Fed Raises Rates
If the Fed delivers a 25-basis-point increase without signalling more aggressive tightening, markets may remain volatile but relatively stable.
Investors will focus on future policy guidance.
$BNB  and $ETH  will need confirmation from spot demand and trading volume.
$PEPE  may remain vulnerable to sudden liquidity changes.
Scenario C — Bearish: Inflation Stays Persistent
If inflation remains elevated and the Fed signals additional tightening, the dollar and Treasury yields could strengthen.
Defensive assets may attract more capital.
Altcoin valuations could face pressure.
Leveraged positions may become vulnerable to liquidation.
PEPE could experience sharper downside volatility.
8. My Investment Strategy: Follow the Capital, Not the Hype
I would not chase a short-term rally simply because the market reacts positively to one headline.
For BNB and ETH, I would look for confirmation through spot demand, trading volume and institutional flows.
For PEPE, I would be more cautious and closely monitor funding rates, open interest and liquidation risks.
My approach would be straightforward:
Build positions gradually rather than committing all capital at once.
Set stop-loss levels before entering a trade.
Avoid excessive leverage.
Monitor Treasury yields and dollar strength.
Distinguish a temporary price rally from a genuine improvement in market structure.
The goal is not to predict every market move. It is to identify where capital is moving and manage risk before market conditions change.
Final Analysis: The Next Crypto Opportunity May Depend on the Fed
The October CPI report is a reminder that cryptocurrency markets do not operate in isolation.
Decisions made in Washington can influence Treasury yields, the dollar, energy prices and international capital flows. Those changes eventually reach crypto markets.
For BNB, the question is whether ecosystem demand can remain strong under tighter financial conditions.
For ETH, it is whether institutional participation and blockchain infrastructure demand can offset higher borrowing costs.
For PEPE, it comes down to whether speculative liquidity remains available when investors become more cautious.
My view is that investors should keep three indicators on their radar: US Treasury yields, dollar strength and institutional crypto flows.
The most important signal will not necessarily be the December rate increase itself. It will be whether the Fed suggests that restrictive monetary policy must continue beyond December.
The best opportunities often emerge when investors understand where capital is moving before the broader market catches up.
What is your strongest investment conviction right now: BNB for ecosystem utility, ETH for institutional adoption, or PEPE for speculative upside? If the Fed raises rates again in December, which one would you be comfortable holding—and why?

title: 杠杆到底是啥？100U怎么撬动1000U，代价是什么
subTitle:
很多刚进场的朋友问我：10倍杠杆是不是就是赚10倍？今天用大白话讲清楚。

【本质】杠杆是交易所借钱给你开仓。你有100U本金，开10倍杠杆，实际控
制的是1000U的仓位。币价涨1%，你的本金赚10%（相对本金）；反过来，
跌1%，本金亏10%——注意，亏损是按你借来的总仓位算的。

【代价】10倍杠杆下，币价反向走约10%，你的本金就归零，这叫爆仓。不是
跌10%才亏完，是跌约10%就全部没了（准确点位还和保证金率有关）。
杠杆放大的不是你的胜率，是波动。方向对，它加速你赚钱；方向错，它加速
你出局。工具没好坏，取决于你有没有把它当工具，而不是当赌具。

【新手建议】先用2-3倍感受波动，把止损练成肌肉记忆，再谈放大。

你怎么看？评论区聊聊你的经历。
#杠杆 #合约 #BTC #ETH

translatedData.title: What exactly is leverage? How can 100 U control 1,000 U, and what’s the cost?
translatedData.subTitle:
A lot of people who are new to trading ask me: Does 10x leverage mean you make 10 times as much? Let me explain it in plain English.

【The basics】Leverage means the exchange lends you money to open a position. If you have 100 U of your own money and use 10x leverage, you actually control
a 1,000 U position. If the coin price rises 1%, you make 10% on your principal. Conversely,
A 1% drop means a 10% loss on your principal—remember, losses are calculated based on the total position you borrowed to open.

【The cost】With 10x leverage, if the coin price moves against you by about 10%, your principal is wiped out. This is called liquidation. It’s not
that you only lose everything after a 10% drop; at around 10%, it’s all gone (the exact threshold also depends on the margin ratio).

ETH Faces Discussion of DeFi Regulation in Japan | Meeting Minutes Are Still Seeking Public Comment | Waiting for Confirmation from Fund Flows and Price

I remain cautiously neutral on ETH. A discussion titled #JapanFSAStudyGroupDiscussesDeFiRegulation is appearing on Binance Square. After checking the Japan Financial Services Agency’s original pages, I think this is worth monitoring, but it must not be presented as “Japan has passed a new DeFi law.” The FSA’s “Study Group on Digital and Decentralized Finance” page lists the minutes of its first meeting on October 20 and materials for its second meeting on November 2. The minutes of the first meeting record hearings with Nomura Holdings and Securitize Japan, and show that stablecoins, tokenized assets, DEXs and DeFi, and wallet service providers were among the topics discussed. Participants noted the need to consider anti-money-laundering measures, investor protection, market integrity, and the authority to respond to incidents. These were discussion points raised by the study group, not formally implemented restrictions; nor was any Ethereum protocol announced as approved or banned.

Why does this matter for ETH? Ethereum is an important settlement layer for DeFi applications, and regulatory boundaries may affect whether Japanese institutions are willing to deploy on-chain assets, wallets, and liquidity services. If future rules enable compliant institutions to connect clearly, that could potentially increase demand for on-chain settlement over the long term. If liability and anti-money-laundering requirements cannot be put into practice, however, project development could be delayed. But there is still a gap between discussion and implementation, involving legislation, licensing, technical audits, and market adoption. Meeting minutes cannot be directly translated into new buying pressure for ETH. My independent view is that, in the short term, we should first monitor policy wording and actual fund flows, while distinguishing among three different signals: public on-chain transaction volume, ETF subscriptions, and spot prices on exchanges.

The market has not yet shown a clear breakout. When I checked, Binance ETHUSDT’s 24-hour statistics were around $2,056.82, down about 1.63% over 24 hours, with a range of $2,006 to $2,109.09. Farside’s tally showed net outflows of about $1.3 million from U.S. spot ETH ETFs on November 10, a sharp narrowing from about $184.6 million on the 9th. But a narrowing in a single day does not mean the institutional trend has reversed, and it would also be inaccurate to say that the Japanese study group caused this price movement. I’m watching the range high near $2,109, the contested area around $2,050, and the range low at $2,006. If ETH breaks above $2,109 but quickly falls back below $2,050, the bullish outlook will not hold. If it loses $2,006 on rising volume, the risk assessment will need to be revisited.

If I were trading myself, I would stay out for now and only consider a leveraged-free spot long. I would wait for ETH to hold above $2,110 on rising volume, then hold the $2,085–$2,110 range on a retest before investing no more than 1.5% of my total capital. I would first take half off at $2,160, reduce further at $2,220, and close the remaining position if the price falls back below $2,110. I would set a hard stop at $2,040 and keep the planned loss on the trade to around 0.05% of my total capital. If the price breaks directly below $2,006, I would not buy the dip on the basis of “regulatory good news.” If the Japan FSA later announces formal rules or a clear timeline, I will check the original text again and adjust my view.

#JapanFSAStudyGroupDiscussesDeFiRegulation #ETH

ETH遇日本DeFi监管讨论｜会议纪要仍是征询意见｜我等资金与价格确认

我对ETH保持谨慎中性。币安广场正出现#JapanFSAStudyGroupDiscussesDeFiRegulation讨论，我核对日本金融厅原始页面后，认为这件事值得跟踪，但绝不能写成“日本已经通过DeFi新法”。金融厅“数字和去中心化金融”研究会页面列出10月20日第一场会议的纪要及11月2日第二场资料。第一场纪要记录了野村控股、Securitize Japan参与听证，并把稳定币、代币化资产、DEX与DeFi、钱包服务商等纳入讨论。与会意见提到要考虑反洗钱、投资者保护、市场健全性和事故时的处置权限；这些是研究会的讨论要点，并非正式实施的限制条款，也没有宣布某条以太坊协议获批或被禁。

为什么这与ETH有关？以太坊是DeFi应用的重要结算层，监管边界会影响日本机构是否愿意部署链上资产、钱包和流动性服务。如果未来规则允许合规机构清晰接入，长期可能提高链上结算需求；若责任与反洗钱要求无法落地，则可能延缓项目推进。不过讨论到业务落地之间还有立法、牌照、技术审计和市场采用的距离，不能把一份纪要直接折算成ETH新增买盘。我的独立判断是，短期先观察政策措辞与资金真实流向，尤其区分公开链上交易量、ETF申购与交易所现货价格三种不同信号。

市场目前没有给出明确突破。币安ETHUSDT的24小时统计在我查看时约2056.82美元，24小时跌约1.63%，区间2006至2109.09美元。Farside汇总的11月10日美国现货ETH ETF净流出约130万美元，较9日约1.846亿美元明显收窄，但单日收窄不代表机构趋势已经逆转，也不能说日本研究会导致了这段价格变化。我关注2109美元的区间上沿、2050美元附近的争夺区和2006美元下沿。若上破2109却很快跌回2050下方，转强判断不成立；若失守2006且放量，则要重新审视风险。

如果是我自己交易，现在不参与，只考虑无杠杆现货试多。等ETH放量站稳2110美元，并在回踩2085至2110区间时守住，再投入总资金最多1.5%；目标先看2160美元减半，再看2220美元继续减仓，剩余仓位跌回2110下方即平仓。硬止损设在2040美元，单笔计划亏损控制在总资金约0.05%以内。若直接跌破2006，我不会为“监管利好”抄底；若日本金融厅之后公布正式规则或明确时间表，我会重新核对原文，再调整判断。

#JapanFSAStudyGroupDiscussesDeFiRegulation #ETH
以上仅为个人市场观察，不构成投资建议。

Want to use the same bank or e-wallet in Europe to buy and sell U.S. stocks and custody Bitcoin? What’s new today is just one more license—not a button that’s already gone live.

On November 11, the Bank of Lithuania (Lietuvos bankas) issued a press release confirming that it had authorized UAB DriveWealth Europe, the European subsidiary of U.S. brokerage infrastructure company DriveWealth, to provide crypto-asset services under the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA). The company made its own announcement first, on November 10; the public register lists November 9 as the start date for the relevant crypto business.

A few points that matter directly to everyday users 👇

🔹 Scope of authorization: The central bank says the company can provide custody and administration of crypto-assets, as well as execute, receive, and transmit crypto-asset orders on behalf of clients. This builds on the financial intermediary (MiFID II) license it obtained in October 2024, meaning the same EU entity is subject to both securities and crypto regulations.

🔹 Not a new app for retail customers: DriveWealth provides “brokerage as a service” to banks, fintech companies, e-wallets, and brokerages. Everyday users won’t be able to open an account and buy crypto directly through its own interface just because of today’s authorization. If a bank or wallet you already use connects to this infrastructure in the future, you may be able to see stocks, tokenized assets, and crypto-assets in the same investment interface.

🔹 Not available yet: The company says crypto-asset services will be rolled out to partners in phases next year, with timing and coverage to be announced separately. It is still building the infrastructure. What the central bank announced today is a license—not a trading or custody feature that’s already live.

🔹 Don’t confuse “authorized to provide services in the EU” with “available to buy across Europe”: The company describes this authorization as a compliant route to providing crypto-asset services in the EU. But there is no timeline yet for when partners will launch or which countries’ users will get access first.

In short: Europe’s regulatory landscape now has another MiCA license, making it easier for banks and wallets to connect crypto-assets to their existing securities infrastructure in the future. It does not mean that everyday users can start depositing or withdrawing Bitcoin through their bank app today. What’s really worth watching is which institutions connect first when the phased rollout begins next year, which assets they will support for custody and trading, and how redemptions and transfers will work.

If you use a bank or e-wallet in Europe to trade U.S. stocks, would you be more interested if it added crypto-assets, or would you still stick with a separate exchange account?

content:
想在欧洲用同一家银行或电子钱包，既买卖美股，又托管比特币？今天多出来的，只是牌照这一步，不是已经上线的按钮。

11月11日，立陶宛央行（Lietuvos bankas）发布新闻稿确认：已经授权美国券商基础设施公司 DriveWealth 的欧洲子公司 UAB DriveWealth Europe，在欧盟《加密资产市场监管条例》（MiCA）下提供加密资产服务。公司自己是 11 月 10 日先宣布的；央行公开登记里，相关加密业务的起始日写的是 11 月 9 日。

几个和普通人直接相关的点👇

🔹 授权范围：央行明确，该公司可以提供加密资产的托管与管理，也可以代客户执行、接收和转递加密资产订单。这是建立在它 2024 年 10 月已拿到的金融中介（MiFID II）牌照之上，同一家欧盟实体同时受证券和加密两套规则约束。

🔹 不是面向个人的新 App：DriveWealth 做的是对银行、金融科技公司、电子钱包和券商的「经纪即服务」。普通人不会因为今天这份授权，就直接在它自己的界面里开户买币；以后若你常用的银行或钱包接入了这条通道，才可能在同一套投资界面里看到股票、代币化资产和加密资产。

🔹 现在还不能用：公司说，加密资产服务将在明年分阶段向合作伙伴开放，具体时间和覆盖范围要另行公布。它正在搭建基础设施，央行今天公布的是许可，不是已经上线的交易或托管按钮。

🔹 别把「可在欧盟提供」听成「全欧洲已经能买」：公司把这份授权表述为可在欧盟提供加密资产服务的合规路径，但合作伙伴何时上线、哪些国家的用户先用上，目前都还没有时间表。

说白了：这是欧洲监管侧又多了一张 MiCA 牌照，方便银行和钱包以后把加密资产接到现有证券通道上，并不是今天起普通人就能在银行 App 里充提比特币。真正要盯的，是明年分阶段开放时，哪些机构先接入、能托管和交易哪些资产、以及赎回和转出怎么走。

如果你在欧洲用银行或电子钱包交易美股，会更在意它以后会不会加上加密资产，还是仍然只用独立的交易所账户？

Last week, the finance minister came forward and said he wanted to discuss with the National Assembly pushing crypto income tax back by another two years. Today, the ruling and opposition parties gave the proposal a tentative nod at the Assembly’s tax subcommittee—but the amendment itself has not yet been put to a vote.

After a meeting of the National Assembly’s Strategy and Finance Committee tax subcommittee on November 11, ruling party secretary and subcommittee chair Oh Ki-hyung (吴基炯) told reporters that the ruling and opposition parties had reached a consensus on further postponing virtual asset taxation. The government had previously said it wanted to delay it by two years, and there was no significant disagreement between the parties. Opposition party secretary Bae Jun-young (裴俊英) also said, “The decision today was to postpone it,” but added that the government must make thorough preparations for taxation during the grace period, and that the National Assembly would monitor its progress.

A few points that directly affect ordinary people 👇

🔹 How far back: If the proposal is ultimately adopted, the virtual asset income tax, originally scheduled to take effect on January 1, 2027, will be delayed by another two years, to 2029. This would be the fourth postponement since the law was enacted in 2020 (it was previously pushed back from 2022 to 2023, 2025, and 2027).

🔹 How much you pay has not changed: The current framework remains in place—the portion of annual gains above approximately 2.5 million won is taxed at about 22% (including local income tax). What is being postponed is the start date, not the tax being eliminated.

🔹 No vote today: The amendment to the Income Tax Act that would “delay it by another two years” was only tentatively agreed on at the tax subcommittee today; it was not formally approved. Oh Ki-hyung said the final vote would be held on the last day of the subcommittee’s work. He also noted, “Given the current situation, it would be fair to say it has already been delayed by two years”—that was an assessment made at the meeting, not a change to the law that has already taken effect.

🔹 Details still unresolved: The government opposes raising the basic deduction (on fairness grounds), and the two sides agreed to continue discussions. They also need to review and decide whether exchanges should submit transaction data in advance of the start date for a system trial. The government’s proposal on November 5 to allow losses to be carried forward for up to three years was on today’s agenda, but no conclusion was reached. Oh Ki-hyung said there was still room for both sides to discuss it constructively.

Put simply: compared with last week’s “government seeks postponement,” things moved a step forward today—the ruling and opposition parties reached a tentative consensus at the first legislative hurdle. But for people trading virtual assets in South Korea, the January 1, 2027 date still needs to be changed, and that will have to wait until the tax subcommittee formally approves the amendment and the remaining National Assembly procedures are completed. Don’t mistake “tentative” for “you won’t have to pay,” and don’t rush to sell everything on the assumption that tax will definitely apply in 2027. Keeping an eye on the amendment text is more reliable than following the headlines.

Will you take today’s “tentative” agreement as a reason to put tax planning aside for now, or wait until the tax subcommittee’s final-day vote before deciding what to do?

content:
上周是财政部长出面，说想跟国会商量、把加密所得税再往后推两年。今天，朝野两边在国会税小委上把这事点了头——不过修法文本还没投票。

11月11日，国会财政经济企划委员会税制小组委员会开完会后，执政党干事、小委员长오기형（吴基炯）对记者说：虚拟资产征税再延期，朝野已经有了共识；政府此前已表态要拖两年，两边没有明显分歧。在野党干事배준영（裴俊英）也说，「结果今天是决定延期了」，但政府必须在宽限期内把征税准备做扎实，国会也会盯进度。

几个和普通人直接相关的点👇

🔹 拖到哪一年：若最终落成，原定2027年1月1日开征的虚拟资产所得税，将再推两年，目标改到2029年。这会是2020年立法以来的第四次延期（此前已从2022拖到2023、2025、2027）。

🔹 交多少没改：现行框架仍是——年收益超过约250万韩元的部分，按约22%（含地方所得税）计征。推迟的是开征日，不是税率清零。

🔹 今天没表决：写入「再拖两年」的所得税法修订案，今天在税小委只是暂定共识，并没有完成议决。吴基炯说，最终表决留到税小委最后一天；他也提到，「以现在的情况，看成已经拖了两年也无妨」——这是现场判断，还不是已经改掉的法律。

🔹 还没谈拢的细则：政府反对上调基本扣除额（理由是公平性），双方约定继续谈；开征前要不要让交易所提前提交交易资料、用来做系统演练，细节也要再核对后再定；政府11月5日提出的「亏损最多结转3年」，今天上了议程，但没有结论，吴基炯说两边都还有积极讨论的空间。

说白了：比起上周「政府寻求延期」，今天往前走了一步——朝野在立法第一关形成了暂定共识。但对在韩国国内所交易的人来说，2027年元旦那一行要改掉，还得等税小委正式通过、后续国会程序走完。别把「暂定」听成「已经不用交」，也别按2027必征去匆忙清仓。盯修法文本，比盯标题更靠谱。

你会把今天的「暂定」当成可以先不管税务规划，还是等税小委最后一天投票再做打算？

SEC enforcement actions decline in number but become more focused

Claims that the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission’s (SEC) enforcement activity decreased in fiscal year 2026 require first clarifying the basis of measurement. The SEC has not yet released an official enforcement report for that fiscal year. External studies do not all calculate the total number of cases in exactly the same way, but they broadly point in the same direction: enforcement actions fell from the previous fiscal year. One compilation found that, excluding follow-on administrative proceedings related to prior cases, there were 232 standalone enforcement actions in fiscal year 2026, down from 303 in fiscal year 2025—a decline of nearly 25%. Including follow-on proceedings, the annual total was 308 actions, a low not seen since at least 2018.

The decline in numbers does not mean regulators are stepping back. There were 122 standalone and follow-on enforcement actions in the first half of the year, down from 146 in the same period a year earlier. But the number rose to 163 in the second half, compared with 69 in the first half, indicating that activity was lower earlier in the year and higher later on. External analyses also note that cases were more concentrated in four areas: securities offerings; issuer reporting and auditing; investment advisers and funds; and insider trading. Together, these accounted for about 88% of activity for the year.

This shift is consistent with the SEC’s publicly stated enforcement approach. Regulators have stressed that case counts are not the sole objective, and that resources will be prioritized for fraud, market manipulation, abuse of trust, and conduct that causes significant harm to investors. The enforcement manual revised in February 2026 formalized procedural transparency and efficiency: recipients of Wells notices generally have four weeks to submit a statement, and related meetings are to be scheduled within four weeks of receiving the materials. Settlement offers and related applications for exemption may be considered at the same time.

For the crypto market, the impact is mainly on expectations rather than on any single number. If enforcement resources continue to focus on fraud, manipulation, violations targeting retail investors, and misuse of customer assets, projects’ disclosures, custody arrangements, marketing claims, and trading practices will remain key areas of compliance scrutiny. By contrast, clearer regulatory procedures and more predictable timelines may ease concerns about regulatory uncertainty, but do not mean that scrutiny of high-risk conduct is weakening.

The editorial view is that the nearly 25% year-over-year decline should be treated as an approximate figure based on external statistics, not as an official SEC finding. More important to watch is whether future official data confirms the trend, and whether enforcement further shifts from broad coverage toward targeted action against conduct that causes core harms.

#SEC FY2026 enforcement actions down 24% #BTC #ETH #BNB

content:
SEC年度执法数量走低但重点更集中

美国证券交易委员会2026财年执法活动减少的说法，需先区分统计口径。SEC截至目前尚未发布该财年的官方执法年度报告；外部研究对案件总量的计算并不完全一致，但方向大致相同：执法数量较上一财年下降。其中一项汇总显示，剔除针对既往案件的后续行政程序后，2026财年共有232宗独立执法行动，低于2025财年的303宗，降幅接近25%。若计入后续程序，全年行动数为308宗，处于至少2018年以来的低位。

数量回落不等于监管退出。上半年曾有122宗独立及后续执法行动，低于上年同期的146宗；但下半年行动数升至163宗，高于上半年的69宗，显示全年节奏存在前低后高的特征。外部分析还指出，案件更集中于证券发行、发行人报告与审计、投资顾问和基金、内幕交易四类领域，占全年活动约88%。

这一变化与SEC公开表述的执法思路相呼应。监管层强调不以案件数量作为唯一目标，而是将资源优先投向欺诈、市场操纵、滥用信任及造成较大投资者损害的行为。2026年2月修订的执法手册，则将程序透明度和处理效率制度化：Wells通知接收方通常有四周提交陈述，相关会议也将安排在收到材料后四周内举行；和解建议及相关豁免申请可被同步审议。

对加密市场而言，影响路径主要在预期而非单一数字。若执法资源继续向欺诈、操纵、面向零售投资者的违法行为及客户资产滥用集中，项目的信息披露、托管安排、营销表述和交易行为仍将是合规审视重点。相对而言，监管程序更明确、处置节奏更可预期，可能降低市场对规则不确定性的担忧，但并不意味着对高风险行为的审查减弱。

编辑判断是，近25%的同比降幅应被视为基于外部统计的近似描述，而非SEC正式定论。更值得持续观察的是后续官方数据是否验证该趋势，以及执法案件是否进一步从广覆盖转向对核心损害行为的定点处理。

title: A CRYPTO PROJECT CAN HAVE 100,000 FOLLOWERS AND STILL BE A BAD PROJECT!
subTitle:
Before getting excited about a new cryptocurrency project, remember this: Popularity is not proof of legitimacy, and marketing is not proof of value. A project may look impressive online, but what happens when you investigate it? Here are 5 things worth checking:
1️⃣ WHO IS BEHIND THE PROJECT?
Can you identify the team, their experience, and their previous work? Anonymous teams are not automatically fraudulent, but they require additional caution.
2️⃣ DOES THE PROJECT SOLVE A REAL PROBLEM?
Look beyond impressive promises. What is it actually building, and who benefits from using it?
3️⃣ IS THERE EVIDENCE OF DEVELOPMENT?
Check its official documentation, product updates, GitHub activity where relevant, and independently verifiable progress.
4️⃣ ARE THE CLAIMS SUPPORTED BY FACTS?
Don't accept screenshots, influencer promotions, or testimonials as sufficient evidence. Verify important claims independently.
5️⃣ WHAT ARE THE RISKS AND WARNING SIGNS?
Investigate token distribution, supply unlocks, liquidity, security audits where relevant, and the project's limitations.
💡 TODAY'S LESSON:
Don't confuse a popular project with a proven project.  Don't confuse a professional website with a trustworthy business.  And don't confuse excitement with evidence.

In Turkey, you still can’t use stablecoins to pay directly in shops, and redemption rules for issuers have not yet been legislated separately. This is the gap the Financial Stability Board highlighted today.

On November 11, the Financial Stability Board (FSB) published its second peer review report on Turkey, assessing the country’s progress in implementing recommendations on crypto-asset and stablecoin regulation. The report recognized that Turkey has brought most crypto-asset businesses within the regulatory perimeter: crypto-asset service providers must register and obtain licenses, customer assets must be segregated and held in custody, and a centralized data platform has been set up for monitoring. The country has also banned the use of crypto-assets for payments and blocked some risks from spilling over into the payments and banking systems. However, a dedicated regime for stablecoin issuers has yet to be established.

A few points that directly affect ordinary people 👇

🔹 Can you spend them in shops? Not yet. The Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye’s (CBRT) 2021 rule prohibiting the use of crypto-assets for payments remains in force. Payment institutions cannot use crypto-assets for payment or e-money services, and licensed payment and e-money institutions cannot facilitate fund transfers for crypto trading, custody, or transfer platforms. Fiat on- and off-ramps are still handled mainly by banks.

🔹 Are there transfer limits? Yes. Authorities have set crypto-to-crypto transfer limits for stablecoins of $3,000 per day and $50,000 per month. Corporate clients may receive time-limited exemptions, subject to approval by the service provider’s board of directors and enhanced due diligence.

🔹 Can they be redeemed, and who oversees the reserves? There are currently no rules specifically for issuers. The management of reserves, how redemption rights are enforced, and how stabilization mechanisms should be designed have not yet been legislated separately. Stablecoin holders are also not covered by the Savings Deposit Insurance Fund (SDIF).

🔹 The e-money route is not yet open: The report says recent revisions to e-money rules allow some fiat-linked stablecoins to be treated as e-money, leaving open a possible path for their future use in payments. But the implementing rules still need to be issued separately by the CBRT, so this does not mean they can already be spent in shops. The FSB also recommends maintaining the firewall against using foreign-currency stablecoins for domestic payments, even if a dedicated regime is introduced.

Today’s report contains peer review recommendations; it is not a new authorization or ban passed by Turkey today. The FSB wants Turkey to establish a dedicated stablecoin regime (including redemption rights, reserve and prudential requirements), implement financial stability monitoring, strengthen regulatory enforcement, and prepare for cross-border cooperation. The progress data cited in the report is current through August 2026.

If you use fiat-backed stablecoins in Turkey, which matters more to you: how future redemption and reserve rules will be written, or whether the domestic payment ban will be eased through the e-money channel?

#FSB敦促土耳其建立稳定币框架 #BTC #ETH

content:
在土耳其，稳定币现在还不能直接拿去店里付款，发行人这一侧的赎回规则也还没单独立法。金融稳定理事会今天点名的，就是这块空档。

11月11日，金融稳定理事会（FSB）发布对土耳其的第二次同行评审报告，评估该国落实加密资产和稳定币监管建议的进展。报告肯定土耳其已把大部分加密业务划进监管圈：加密资产服务商要注册许可、客户资产要隔离托管，并建了集中数据平台做监测；境内禁止用加密资产付款，也挡住了一部分风险向支付和银行体系传导。但针对稳定币发行人的专门制度，目前仍未建立。

几个和普通人直接相关的点👇

🔹 店里能不能花：现在还是不行。土央行（CBRT）2021 年「加密资产不得用于支付」的规定仍有效——支付机构不能把加密资产做成支付或电子货币业务，持牌支付和电子货币机构也不能给加密交易、托管或转账平台做资金划转，出入金仍主要由银行经办。

🔹 转账有没有额度：有。当局把稳定币的加密对加密转账限额设在每日 3000 美元、每月 5 万美元；企业客户可经各服务商董事会批准，在加强尽职调查后获得限期例外。

🔹 能不能兑、储备谁管：目前没有专门针对发行人的规则，储备怎么管、赎回权怎么落实、稳定机制如何设计，都还没有单独立法。稳定币持有人也不在储蓄存款保险基金（SDIF）的保障范围内。

🔹 电子货币这条路还没走通：报告写到，近期电子货币规则修订允许把部分挂钩法币的稳定币视同电子货币，为将来用于支付留了一条可能路径；但实施细则要等土央行另行制定，现在不能当成已经能在店里花。FSB 同时建议，即便补上专门制度，也要继续守住「外币稳定币不拿来做境内支付」的防火墙。

今天这份报告是同行评审建议，不是土耳其当天新通过的开闸或禁令。FSB 希望土方建立专门的稳定币制度（含赎回权、储备和审慎要求）、落实金融稳定监测、加强监管执法，并做好跨境合作。报告依据的进展数据截至 2026 年 8 月。

如果你在土耳其使用法币稳定币，更关心以后赎回和储备规则怎么写，还是境内支付禁令会不会通过电子货币通道松动？

Simmons never predicts the market; he just crunches the numbers. An annualized return of 66% over thirty years came from countless tiny, repeatable edges. The problem with retail traders is that every time, they’re looking for the one answer that will make them ten times their money.

Take today’s $ETH , for example: it’s at 2,062, down 1.52% over 24 hours. This kind of market action is a perfect illustration of the point above. It’s no coincidence—it’s human nature repeating itself in the charts.

The more I think about it, the more I feel that in the end, trading isn’t about technical skill—it’s about mindset.
Making a note of this to look back on later.

title: ETH和Gas费：一条链的油钱是怎么回事
subTitle:
转账要交Gas费、mint个NFT要Gas费，这钱付给谁了？

【本质】以太坊是一台全球共享的计算机，每笔操作（转账、交易、跑
合约）都要消耗计算资源。Gas就是你付给帮你执行计算的验证者的
「油钱」。网络越堵，大家抢着执行，油价（Gas单价）越高。

【为什么和币价有关】行情火爆→链上交易暴增→Gas费飙升。所以老玩家
有个习惯：链上操作挑深夜或行情冷清的时候，同样的操作能省一半钱。

【和投资的关联】Gas费水平是链上活跃度的实时温度计。持续高Gas=
链上需求旺盛；长期冷清=应用使用减少。把它当链上情绪的辅助观察，
挺有意思。

translatedData.title: ETH and Gas Fees: What Are a Blockchain’s Fuel Costs?
translatedData.subTitle:
You pay gas fees to transfer funds and to mint an NFT. Who gets that money?

【The basics】Ethereum is a globally shared computer. Every operation (transfers, trades, running
contracts) consumes computing resources. Gas is what you pay the validators who perform those computations for you.
“Fuel costs.” The more congested the network, the more people compete to get their transactions processed, and the higher the gas price (the price per unit of gas).

【Why it’s related to token prices】A hot market → a surge in on-chain transactions → skyrocketing gas fees. That’s why seasoned users
have a habit: they choose late at night or quiet market periods for on-chain activity. The same operations can cost half as much.

In South Korea, it’s still not possible to send money abroad using stablecoins through a bank or card network. Today, the head of the Foreign Exchange Analysis Division at the Ministry of Economy and Finance clarified how responsibilities will be divided: issuance will be governed by the Digital Asset Act, led by the Financial Services Commission, while cross-border payments and receipts will require a separate revision to the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

On the afternoon of November 11, a seminar titled “The Future of Cross-Border Payments in Korea in the Stablecoin Era” was held at Post Tower in Yeouido, Seoul. It was co-hosted by Democratic Party lawmakers Jeong Tae-ho and Ahn Do-geol, and organized by the Korea Fintech Industry Association. At the seminar, Son Seon-young, head of the Foreign Exchange Analysis Division at the Ministry of Economy and Finance, said that matters related to stablecoin issuance would be governed by the Digital Asset Act, which is being discussed under the leadership of the Financial Services Commission, while cross-border transactions using stablecoins are expected to be governed by the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. She also said that, in conjunction with the enactment of the Digital Asset Act, the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act would clarify stablecoins’ legal status, cross-border transactions, and payment and receipt procedures.

A few points that directly affect ordinary people 👇

🔹 This isn’t a new opening approved today, nor is it a new ban: the division chief was describing the direction of the regulatory framework; no amendment text has been released yet. The government plans to first establish issuance rules in the Digital Asset Act, then revise the foreign exchange law accordingly.

🔹 Why can’t banks handle this now? She explained that when the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act was amended this June, it introduced a “virtual asset transfer business” category, mainly to track information on cross-border virtual asset transfers and the movement of funds in and out of the country. Under the current legal framework, small overseas remittance providers, banks, and card companies still cannot transfer stablecoins directly. To do so, they would first have to register as virtual asset transfer businesses.

🔹 Details that will be added to the foreign exchange law: whether stablecoins will be included in the existing category of “means of payment to and from foreign countries” or treated as a separate category; what will be permitted for current-account transactions (trade in goods and services) versus capital-account transactions (investment and movement of funds); and who will verify transactions across borders and what documents will be required. The principle is “same activity, same regulation.” While safeguarding the integrity of foreign exchange transactions, the government will also consider private-sector demand, transaction types, and whether the institutions handling transactions can fulfill their verification obligations.

🔹 This is not the same issue as “how domestic payments will be protected”: which consumer-protection law applies to domestic stablecoin payments is a separate discussion. What the Ministry of Economy and Finance clarified today is that cross-border transfers and remittances will be subject to the foreign exchange law. Neither issue has yet become a set of rules in force.

Put simply: South Korea did not announce today that banks will be able to send money abroad using stablecoins starting tomorrow. But the Ministry of Economy and Finance made clear at the seminar that “cross-border transactions fall under the foreign exchange law, and banks and card networks currently cannot transfer stablecoins directly.” The key question to watch is which institutions will be allowed to handle cross-border payments and receipts, and what procedures they will need to follow, once the Digital Asset Act is enacted—not to mistake the division of responsibilities discussed at the seminar for a new channel that is already available.

Are you more concerned about whether banks and card networks will be able to handle cross-border transactions in the future, or about first clarifying what will be permitted for current-account and capital-account transactions?

#韩国财政部称稳定币跨境支付将适用外汇交易法 #ETH #BTC

content:
在韩国，想通过银行或卡组织用稳定币给国外打一笔钱，现在还过不去。财政经济部外汇分析课课长今天把分管线讲清楚了：发行走金融委员会主导的《数字资产法》，跨境收付要另修《外汇交易法》。

11月11日下午，首尔汝矣岛 Post Tower 举行「稳定币时代，韩国跨境支付的未来」研讨会，由共同民主党郑太浩、安道杰议员共同主办、韩国金融科技产业协会承办。财政经济部外汇分析课课长손선영在会上表示，稳定币发行相关事项将由以金融委员会为中心讨论的《数字资产法》规范，用稳定币做跨境交易则预定由《外汇交易法》规范。她还说，将结合《数字资产法》的制定，在《外汇交易法》里明确稳定币的法律性质、跨境交易以及收付款程序。

几个和普通人直接相关的点👇

🔹 这不是今天新通过的开放令，也不是新禁令：课长讲的是制度安排方向，修订文本还没拿出来。政府要先把《数字资产法》里的发行规则定下来，再连着改外汇法。

🔹 现在银行为什么办不了：她解释，今年 6 月修订《外汇交易法》时新设了「虚拟资产转移业者」制度，主要是为了掌握跨境虚拟资产转移的信息和资金进出。按现行法体系，小额海外汇款业者、银行和卡公司都还不能直接转移稳定币，要做的话必须先登记为虚拟资产转移业者。

🔹 接下来会写进外汇法的细节：是否把稳定币纳入现行「对外支付手段」，还是单列一类；经常项目（商品服务贸易）和资本项目（投资、资金移动）分别允许到什么范围；跨境时谁来做交易核验、要准备哪些证明。原则是「同一类型、同一监管」，在守住外汇交易健全性的同时，综合考虑民间需求、交易类型，以及经办机构能不能履行核验义务。

🔹 和「国内付款怎么保护」不是同一件事：国内用稳定币结账适用哪部保护法，是另一条讨论线；今天财政部明确的是跨境转出、汇入要走外汇法。两边都还没变成已经生效的细则。

说白了：韩国并没有在今天宣布银行明天就能用稳定币给国外打款，但「跨境这一段归外汇法管、现在银行和卡组织还不能直接转」已经由财政部当场说清楚了。要盯的是《数字资产法》出台后，外汇法会允许哪些机构、以什么手续做跨境收付，而不是把研讨会上的分工理解成已经能用的新通道。

你更关心以后跨境能不能走银行和卡组织，还是先把经常项目和资本项目分别允许到哪一步写清楚？

In Japan, swapping coins on decentralized exchanges did not result in a new ban today. What the Financial Services Agency made public was the minutes of the first meeting of the “Digital and Distributed Finance Response Study Group” held on October 20: the members wrote into their opinions how DeFi should be regulated, who should act as the gatekeeper, and whether large-scale redemptions of stablecoins could affect government bonds.

A few points directly relevant to ordinary people 👇

🔹 No law has changed yet; the discussion has only been laid out: the meeting lasted two hours on the afternoon of October 20, and Nomura Holdings and Securitize Japan gave hearings. The minutes omit the names of speakers and record the members’ opinions, not rules that are already in force. The same study group held a second meeting on November 2; what is newly added today is the written minutes of the first meeting.

🔹 Who to regulate first for DeFi: members suggested first clarifying “how to deal with decentralized exchanges and DeFi,” while also comparing international discussions to sort out the regulatory targets and methods, so that Japan does not become “a place of regulatory vacuum or regulatory arbitrage,” and to respond appropriately in due course. Investor protection and market integrity were listed as points that should be discussed first. The “gatekeeper” role that traditional financial institutions have long performed was also written into the agenda as something to consider who should bear in the future. On anti-money laundering, members asked for serious discussion of how Japan should treat the FATF’s DeFi report released in July this year.

🔹 The most likely first point of contact for users later: the secretariat materials on the day still followed the organization in the 2025 December working group report—currently, there is no clear regulatory method for the decentralized exchange protocol itself; however, people who provide “application interfaces that connect to decentralized exchanges” to residents in Japan may be considered subject to obligations such as risk explanations and identity verification under the Act on Prevention of Transfer of Criminal Proceeds, and the actual situation of such interfaces needs to be examined first. The materials also state clearly: trading on decentralized exchanges or with operators not registered in Japan carries a risk of users suffering unexpected harm, and administrative bodies and licensed exchanges should provide sufficient notice. This is existing整理, not a new ban passed today.

🔹 Large-scale stablecoin redemptions: members pointed out that if major issuers of electronic payment instruments receive large redemption requests, government bonds held as reserve assets may also have to be sold in large quantities, so it is necessary to confirm whether the current regulations are sufficient. There was also an opinion that lending of electronic payment instruments, if bundled with issuance, may look like investment solicitation, and whether the current rules are adequate deserves another look.

In short: Japan did not announce a ban on using decentralized exchanges today, but questions like “who verifies identity on the front end” and “whether large redemptions will spill over into government bonds” have moved from internal discussion into public minutes. What to watch next is whether these opinions are written into a draft system, rather than treating the minutes as a newly effective rule.

Do you think they should regulate apps that connect to decentralized exchanges first, or should they first add rules to cover the government bond selling pressure during stablecoin redemptions?

#日本金融厅研究会讨论DeFi监管 #ETH #BTC

content:
在日本连去中心化交易所换币，今天并没有多出一条新禁令。金融厅公开的，是 10 月 20 日「数字与分布式金融应对研究会」第一次会议的纪要：委员把 DeFi 怎么管、谁来当守门人、稳定币大额赎回会不会牵动国债，都写进了意见。

几个和普通人直接相关的点👇

🔹 还没改法，只是把讨论摊开了：这场会 10 月 20 日下午开了两个小时，野村控股和 Securitize Japan 做了听证。纪要隐去了发言人姓名，记录的是委员意见，不是已经生效的规则。同一研究会 11 月 2 日开过第二次会；今天新增的，是第一次会的书面纪要。

🔹 DeFi 先管谁：委员提出，先把「怎么和去中心化交易所、DeFi 相处」谈清楚，同时要对照国际讨论，整理监管对象和手法，避免日本变成「监管空白或监管套利的地方」，并适时应对。投资人保护、市场健全性被列为应优先讨论的点；传统金融机构一直在做的「守门人」角色，以后由谁来担，也写进了议题。反洗钱方面，委员要求认真讨论日本应如何对待今年 7 月金融行动特别工作组（FATF）的 DeFi 报告。

🔹 用户以后最可能先碰到的切口：当天秘书处资料仍沿用 2025 年 12 月工作组报告的整理——目前对去中心化交易所协议本身，还没有明确的监管手法；但向日本境内居民提供「连接去中心化交易所的应用界面」的人，会被考虑课以风险说明、以及犯罪收益转移防止法上的本人确认等义务，先要摸清这类界面的实际情况。资料也写明：在去中心化交易所、或未在日本注册的业者处交易，存在使用者遭受不测损害的风险，行政和持牌交易所等应充分告知。这是既有整理，不是今天新通过的禁令。

🔹 稳定币大额赎回：委员指出，如果电子支付手段的大规模发行者接到大额赎回请求，作为后备资产的国债也可能被大量卖掉，因此有必要确认现有监管是否够用。还有意见认为，电子支付手段的借贷若和发行捆在一起提供，看起来也像投资劝诱，现行规则够不够值得再看。

说白了：日本没有在今天宣布禁止使用去中心化交易所，但「前端谁来核验身份、大额赎回会不会传导到国债」已经从内部讨论变成了公开纪要。接下来要盯的，是这些意见会不会写进制度草案，而不是把纪要当成已经生效的新规。

你觉得该先把连接去中心化交易所的应用管起来，还是先把稳定币赎回时的国债抛压补上规则？

Deutsche Bank Plans to Launch Crypto Custody Services in Germany

Deutsche Bank is bringing its digital asset business into its corporate banking services framework. According to reports, the bank plans to launch crypto asset custody services in Germany in the coming weeks, with a view to expanding the services to Asia in 2027. It is worth noting that the German business is still subject to regulatory approval. At this stage, it is therefore more accurate to say that the services are being prepared for launch and planned for expansion, rather than already being fully operational.

The initial range of assets the service is expected to support includes Bitcoin, Ethereum, and stablecoins such as USDC, EURC, and EURAU. The core arrangement is for the bank to manage clients’ digital wallets and private keys, enabling corporate and institutional clients to hold and transfer these assets while leaving key custody, wallet security, and related technical operations to the bank. Reports also say the bank plans to develop stablecoin exchange services and tokenized deposits, and to help clients issue digital bonds and other blockchain-based securities.

The significance of this initiative lies not simply in adding more assets to the range available for custody, but in combining traditional banking strengths—account management, risk-control processes, and compliance governance—with digital asset infrastructure. For some institutions, building their own wallet management systems requires ongoing investment in key backups, access controls, internal audits, and operational risk management. If bank custody can operate reliably with regulatory approval and adequate service capabilities, it may lower the operational barriers for these institutions to access digital asset infrastructure. However, custody does not eliminate risk. Clients still need to assess the service terms, asset segregation arrangements, operational security, and applicable regulatory rules.

For the crypto market, the impact of major banks entering the custody business will be felt primarily at the institutional services level. First, custody capabilities can give institutions a more familiar framework for holding and transferring digital assets. Second, related plans for stablecoin exchange, tokenized deposits, and digital bonds may foster closer links between stablecoins and on-chain securities services. Third, if the planned expansion into Asia goes ahead, institutions in the region may have more compliant service providers to choose from. However, the first Asian market to be entered has not yet been disclosed, and further details on specific products, client eligibility, and cross-border rules await confirmation.

The editorial view is that this plan reflects how banks’ interest in digital assets is expanding beyond a single point of access for trading to foundational services such as custody, settlement, and securities issuance. What deserves continued attention is not how many assets the bank announces it will support, but whether its German business secures approval and operates reliably, and whether its expansion into Asia can establish clear, workable compliance and risk management mechanisms.

德意志银行拟在德国启动加密托管服务

德意志银行正将数字资产业务纳入企业银行服务框架。根据报道，该行计划在未来数周内于德国启动加密资产托管服务，并拟于2027年将相关服务拓展至亚洲。需要注意的是，德国业务仍以获得监管批准为前提，因此现阶段更准确的表述是服务处于启动准备及扩展规划中，而非已经全面落地。

在首批资产范围上，服务拟支持比特币、以太坊，以及USDC、EURC和EURAU等稳定币。其核心安排是由银行管理客户数字钱包和私钥，使企业及机构客户能够持有和转移相关资产，同时把密钥保管、钱包安全及相应技术运维交由银行处理。报道还称，该行拟布局稳定币兑换、代币化存款，并协助客户发行数字债券及其他基于区块链的证券。

这一布局的重点并不只是增加可托管的币种，而是将传统银行擅长的账户管理、风控流程、合规治理与数字资产基础设施结合。对部分机构而言，自建钱包管理体系意味着密钥备份、权限设置、内部审计和操作风险控制等持续投入；银行托管若能在监管许可和服务能力上稳定运行，可能降低这些机构接触数字资产基础设施的操作门槛。但托管并不等于风险消失，客户仍需评估服务条款、资产隔离方式、运营安全和适用监管规则。

对加密市场而言，大型银行参与托管的影响路径主要在机构服务层面：其一，托管能力可为机构持有和调拨数字资产提供更熟悉的操作框架；其二，稳定币兑换、代币化存款和数字债券等配套计划，可能推动稳定币与链上证券服务形成更紧密的连接；其三，若亚洲扩展按计划推进，区域内机构可选择的合规服务渠道或将增加。不过，首个进入的亚洲市场尚未披露，具体产品、客户准入和跨境规则仍有待后续信息确认。

编辑观察认为，这项计划反映出银行业对数字资产的关注正从单一交易入口延伸至托管、结算和证券发行等底层服务。真正值得持续关注的，不是宣布覆盖多少资产，而是德国业务能否完成审批并稳定运行，以及亚洲扩展后能否形成清晰、可执行的合规与风险管理机制。

As of the afternoon of November 11 Beijing time, Ethereum was trading at $2,057.60, down about 2.2% over the past 24 hours. 以太坊市场深度分析：两千美元关口的攻防战

一、价格走势分析

截至北京时间十一月十一日下午，以太坊报价两千零五十七点六美元，过去二十四小时下跌约百分之二点二。从小时K线来看，ETH在过去数小时内呈现震荡下行的走势，从两千零七十美元上方逐步回落至两千零五十二美元附近，最低触及两千零五十二美元。价格运行在布林带中轨两千零五十三美元附近，上轨约两千零八十三美元，下轨约两千零二十三点，整体波动区间较比特币更为狭窄。

以太坊面临的宏观压力与比特币类似，美国超预期的CPI数据引发了市场对美联储持续加息的担忧。但ETH还承受着额外的结构性压力。现货以太坊ETF在十一月九日单日流出一亿八千四百六十万美元，十一月十日继续流出一点三亿美元，形成了持续的需求缺口。链上数据显示，高峰期每小时净流出超过三千八百八十万美元，价格一度跌破两千零一十八美元的关键支撑位后才企稳回升。

值得注意的是，尽管价格持续走弱，以太坊的质押比率却攀升至历史新高，达到总供应量的百分之三十六点三二。这表明长期持有者对以太坊的未来依然充满信心，短期价格波动并未动摇他们的持仓意愿。多位链上鲸鱼也在逆势抄底，其中一位资深玩家在两千零三十至两千零六十四美元区间买入了一千四百五十一枚ETH，另一位鲸鱼更是斥资两千两百万美元购入一万零七百九十二枚ETH。

二、技术指标解读

从一小时级别的技术指标来看，MACD指标同样处于负值区域，DIF线约负九点四五，DEA线约负十二点九六，柱状图约三点五一，虽然连续翻红但动能较弱，显示空头力量虽有减弱但反转信号尚不明确。RSI十四周期处于中性偏弱区域，短期RSI六周期降至四十二点一二，已接近超卖区域。

均线系统呈现明显的空头排列。七周期均线约两千零六十二美元，二十五周期均线约两千零六十美元，九十九周期均线高达两千一百五十三美元。价格远低于所有中长期均线，且短期均线正在向下拐头，中期下行趋势明确。EMA七约两千零五十九美元，EMA二十五约两千零六十八美元，EMA九十九约两千一百三十八美元，同样确认了空头格局。

KDJ指标快速走弱，K线降至五十四点六八，D线六十四点一零，J线大幅回落至三十五点八五，已进入相对低位区域。威廉指标从负四点六四恶化至负六十点五八，短线卖压明显。不过ATR指标从十九点三八降至十八点二六，波动率持续收敛，可能预示着方向性突破即将到来。随机RSI从一百的极高位快速回落至七十一点六零，虽然下行趋势明确，但回落速度较快，需警惕超卖后的技术性反弹。

三、市场情绪分析

以太坊市场当前的情绪可以用谨慎中带有分歧来形容。一方面，ETF持续流出和价格走弱打击了短线交易者的信心，部分鲸鱼也在向交易所转入ETH，增加了潜在的卖盘压力。另一方面，质押比率创历史新高和鲸鱼逆势抄底表明，长期持有者对以太坊生态的基本面依然看好。

从生态层面来看，以太坊面临的挑战不仅来自宏观环境。基金会内部的治理争议和升级延迟也对市场信心造成了一定影响。容量升级因安全审计而暂停，叠加法律纠纷，使得部分投资者对以太坊的长期发展路径产生了疑虑。不过，DeFi赛道依然保持活力，PancakeSwap累计交易量突破四点五万亿美元，跨链生态的持续扩展为整个行业提供了基本面支撑。

从ETH与BTC的比价关系来看，以太坊年内表现明显落后于比特币，差距约为二十六个百分点。这种弱势表现部分源于ETF资金流向的分化，但也反映了市场对以太坊生态不确定性的定价。短期内，两千美元是重要的心理和技术支撑位，若能有效守住，可能为反弹奠定基础；若跌破，则可能进一步下探至一千九百五十美元附近。

综合来看，以太坊正处于宏观逆风与生态基本面的博弈之中。短线技术面偏空，但长期持有者的坚定态度和鲸鱼的抄底行为为市场提供了一定的底部支撑。建议投资者控制仓位，关注两千美元关口的得失，等待更明确的方向信号。

Impact on the market
- Short term: For now, this kind of executive activity could have a somewhat negative effect on sentiment around XRP and BTC, as investors may view it as a bearish signal.
- Medium term: In light of industry dynamics and regulatory trends, this event may not have much impact on the medium-term development of the broader cryptocurrency market. At this point, this event looks more like market noise. It may cause some volatility in the short term, but XRP and BTC prices should still be influenced by fundamentals. Deutsche Bank custody plan climbs trending charts | Website still says pending completion of regulatory processes | For ETH, watch for service launch, not expectations

My stance is cautious: I won’t describe “plans to launch” as “already live.” The hashtag #DeutscheBankLaunchesDigitalAssetCustodyForBTCETH appeared on Binance Square’s trending list, directly involving an institutional gateway to Ethereum. I checked Deutsche Bank’s official September 16 press release: it says the bank plans to launch digital asset custody in 2026 for eligible institutional and corporate clients in Europe, with Bitcoin, Ether, and some stablecoins slated for initial support. The onboarding date for the first clients still depends on completion of applicable regulatory processes. The bank’s November 4 article on digital asset custody also emphasized the importance of infrastructure, but did not confirm that the service had officially opened to clients. So I classify this as a credible institutional development plan, not a new source of ETH buying today.

Why can custody affect the crypto market? If institutions can use the banking system to safeguard private keys, carry out multi-party approvals, and segregate assets, their internal risk-control costs may fall, potentially lowering the barriers to allocating to ETH in the future. But custody services only address safekeeping and transfers. They do not guarantee that clients will buy ETH, nor do they automatically generate staking yields or ETF inflows. To see a real impact, we still need the bank to announce the launch, client adoption, and assets under custody, then see whether fund flows follow.

For now, flows offer no strong confirmation. The Farside table shows net outflows of $184.6 million from spot ETH ETFs on November 9 and $1.3 million on November 10. The pressure has eased but flows have not turned positive. U.S. October CPI rose 0.4% month over month, while core CPI rose 0.3%. The Federal Reserve maintained its target interest-rate range, and institutional risk budgets remain constrained by macro conditions. The Ethereum Foundation’s review of Glamsterdam contract compatibility is also ongoing, so the upgrade timeline should await official confirmation.

As for the market reaction, at the time I checked, Kraken’s ETH/USD spot price was around $2,055, with an intraday high of about $2,071 and a low of about $2,041. The price moved within the day’s range, with insufficient evidence to attribute every fluctuation to the Deutsche Bank news. If the price holds above $2,071 and ETF flows turn positive, the short-term outlook could improve. If it falls below $2,041 and fails to recover, that would indicate buying demand remains insufficient. If the bank again explicitly delays the launch or regulatory conditions are not met, expectations for institutional adoption should also be revised downward.

If I were trading this myself, I would sit out for now, remain directionally neutral, hold no position, and use no leverage. Only if ETH/USD closes above $2,075 for two consecutive four-hour candles and the next verifiable ETF daily report shows net inflows would I consider buying spot, using at most 2.5% of my total capital. The entry would be based on the actual trigger price; a plan is not a fill. The first target is $2,110, where I would sell half. The second target is $2,160, where I would reduce the remaining position in stages. I would set the initial stop-loss at $2,035. If the price breaks out and then falls back below $2,071 without recovering by the four-hour close, I would exit. I would also cancel the plan if $2,041 breaks or the bank officially confirms a custody delay. Waiting for the facts to materialize is safer than chasing an unverified “already live” headline.

Sources: Deutsche Bank’s official September 16 press release and November 4 article; Farside’s daily ETH ETF table; the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics’ October CPI report; the Federal Reserve’s October 28 statement; Ethereum Foundation announcements; and Kraken ETH/USD spot market data. #DeutscheBankLaunchesDigitalAssetCustodyForBTCETH #ETH
The above is solely my personal market observation and does not constitute investment advice.

我的态度是谨慎，不把“计划推出”写成“已经上线”。币安广场热榜出现#DeutscheBankLaunchesDigitalAssetCustodyForBTCETH，直接涉及以太坊的机构入口。核对德意志银行9月16日的官方新闻稿，表述是拟于2026年向欧洲合资格机构与企业客户推出数字资产托管，首批拟支持比特币、以太币及部分稳定币；首批客户上线时间仍取决于适用监管流程完成。银行11月4日对数字资产托管的文章也强调基础设施的重要性，却没有给出此项服务已经正式对客户开放的确认。因此我把它归类为可信的机构建设计划，而不是今天新增的ETH买盘。

托管为什么会影响加密市场？机构若能通过银行体系保管私钥、执行多方审批和资产隔离，内部风控成本可能降低，未来配置ETH的门槛可能下降。但托管服务只解决保管和转移，不保证客户一定购买ETH，更不会自动带来质押收益或ETF净流入。要看到真实传导，仍需银行公布上线、客户启用与资产规模，再观察基金资金是否跟随。

眼下资金并未给出强确认。Farside表显示，ETH现货ETF11月9日净流出1.846亿美元，10日净流出130万美元，压力收窄但未转正。美国10月CPI环比上涨0.4%、核心上涨0.3%，美联储维持利率目标区间，机构风险预算仍受宏观约束。以太坊基金会对Glamsterdam合约兼容性的审查也仍在进行，升级时间应等官方确认。

市场反应方面，核对时Kraken的ETH/USD现货约2055美元，当日高点约2071、低点约2041。价格在日内区间里来回，没有足够证据把每一笔波动归因于德银新闻。若价格站稳2071且ETF流向转正，短线判断可以改善；若跌破2041并持续收不回，说明买盘还不足。若银行再次明确延期、监管条件未满足，原本的机构落地预期也应下修。

如果是我自己交易，现在不参与，方向观望，仓位0，不使用杠杆。只有ETH/USD连续两根四小时K线收在2075美元上方，同时下一份可核实的ETF日报转为净流入，我才考虑用总资金最多2.5%买入现货；入场以实际触发价为准，不能把计划当成交。第一目标2110美元，到位减半；第二目标2160美元，余仓分批减仓。初始止损设在2035美元，若突破后又跌回2071下方并四小时收不回就平仓；若2041失守或官方确认托管延期，也取消计划。用条件等信息兑现，比追一个未经证实的“已上线”标题稳妥。

来源：德意志银行9月16日官方新闻稿与11月4日文章、Farside ETH ETF逐日表、美国劳工统计局10月CPI、美联储10月28日声明、以太坊基金会公告、Kraken ETH/USD现货行情。#DeutscheBankLaunchesDigitalAssetCustodyForBTCETH #ETH
以上仅为个人市场观察，不构成投资建议。

title: 交易心理 | 比预测行情更重要的事：复盘你自己的单子
subTitle:

translatedData.title: Trading Psychology | What Matters More Than Predicting the Market: Reviewing Your Own Trades
translatedData.subTitle:
Most people spend 90% of their time predicting the market and 0% reviewing their own performance. They’ve got it backwards.

Write down three things for every trade: why you entered (your rationale), what went right or wrong (execution),
and what you’ll do differently next time (a specific action). Stick with it for a month, and you’ll be shocked to discover: your losses…
The trade log is full of the same mistakes happening over and over—for example, always reversing your position right after a stop-loss,
or never letting winning trades run.

The market changes, but your behavioral patterns won’t change on their own unless you keep an eye on them and work to change them. The market is the most
honest teacher, and your trade history is your report card. Don’t just look at your account balance—go through your trading records.

title: 周四早盘：夜里摸到约 7.48，把昨天下午够不着的约 7.44 收了回来——亚洲早盘又从高点吐了约 1300
subTitle:
公开行情里，昨天下午最高只摸到约 7.42、始终够不着的约 7.44，昨天夜里到凌晨一口气收了回来：23 点从约 7.34 附近往上抬，凌晨 1 点到 5 点最高摸到约 7.48——几乎贴上昨天的 24 小时高点。ETH 更是夜里最高摸到约 2104，把盯了两天的约 2080 也收了一下。结果亚洲早盘一脚，BTC 从约 7.48 滑到 7 点附近约 7.35，吐了约 1300；ETH 从约 2104 掉到约 2036。这会儿 BTC 约 7.40 万（近 24 小时约 +0.8%），高点约 7.48、低点约 7.32；ETH 约 2061（约 +0.6%）又回到约 2080 下方；BNB 约 682（约 +0.3%）继续相对抗跌；SOL 约 83.7（约 +0.6%）、XRP 约 1.057（约 +0.6%）跟了一截，但夜里高点约 85.9 / 约 1.081 也都吐回去了。

周四早盘这个位置，我不把「夜里收回约 7.44、摸到约 7.48」读成已经翻过去了：更刺眼的是，约 7.48 只在凌晨亮了一下，亚洲早盘就把刚抬起来的一千多几乎吐完，又卡回约 7.40——差不多落在昨天傍晚约 7.37 和下午高点约 7.42 之间。约 7.27 那脚新低到现在都没人再踩，说明下方仍有人接；但约 7.44 和约 7.48 这两道刚被摸到的位置，这会儿都还在上头，而且没站住。

结构上我更盯三件事：一是约 7.40 这截早盘位置还站不站得住——若再往下靠近今早约 7.35，说明夜里这截只是回抽；二是约 7.44 / 约 7.48 还回不回得去、进没进得了；三是 ETH 夜里摸到约 2104 之后又掉回约 2061，约 2080 收不收得回来，SOL/XRP 相对波动收不收窄。

我个人怎么读这个周四早盘（仅观察，非投资建议）：

1. 把「傍晚约 7.37 → 夜里约 7.48 → 亚洲早盘约 7.35 → 现约 7.40」当成对约 7.44 的一次夜盘回抽再回落，比当成已经站上约 7.44、转向修复便宜——高点没守住，早盘又回到昨天傍晚附近。
2. 大饼近 24 小时约 +0.8%，ETH/SOL/XRP 也翻到约 +0.6%，BNB 几乎走平约 +0.3%：数字看起来比昨天绿了一些，但都是夜里冲高后吐回来的，不是早盘自己走出来的。
3. 今天的顺序：约 7.40 早盘位置守不守 → 今早约 7.35 还要不要再踩 → 约 7.44 / 约 7.48 还回不回得去 → ETH 约 2080 收不收得回来 → 约 7.27 坑还在不在脚下。

你怎么看：这算「约 7.27 之后夜里能摸到约 7.48，修复的脚已经迈出去了」，还是「约 7.44 和约 7.48 都没站住，只是把压力再确认一遍」？评论区聊聊。

BitPay has launched a cryptocurrency purchasing process that supports Apple Pay and Google Pay, allowing users in Europe to buy crypto quickly with their phones. This is completely different from the old-fashioned approach of manually entering addresses, wallet details, and private keys. Now, all it takes is scanning a code or confirming with a fingerprint—just like paying for things with WeChat Pay or Alipay. This is especially important for cryptocurrency adoption: if everyday people find crypto payments as convenient as cash, they’ll naturally be more willing to try cryptocurrency.

Why does this news matter?
BitPay’s move is significant because it directly addresses the poor user experience that has long plagued cryptocurrency. Buying crypto used to be as much of a hassle as opening a bank account; now, it’s as simple as tapping your phone. This means cryptocurrency is becoming as practical as internet infrastructure. It’s no longer a game for a small circle of enthusiasts, but a tool that can genuinely fit into everyday life. For the industry as a whole, this is a key step in shifting from speculation to practical value. For example, many young people are used to buying coffee with Apple Pay. If crypto payments become just as easy, conversion among younger users could increase significantly.

Impact on the market
Although this news won’t directly push up the price of BTC or ETH, it could have a positive long-term effect on overall market sentiment. A larger user base also means greater liquidity. This news is a boost to sentiment across the crypto market, but it won’t change the price trends of BTC or ETH in the short term. 各位 DragonX 龙币中文社区的小伙伴们：
最近，社区核心团队与首席开发者 Dan Akston 就 DragonX ($DRGX)龙币 的底层技术架构、发展历史、产品体验以及未来的研发路线进行了深度交流。为了让大家更清晰地理解 龙币$DRGX 的核心竞争力与宣发边界，我们对关键技术真相与产品定位做了一次系统性的梳理：
一、 核心竞争力：不是“拥有 zk”，而是“强制隐私（Privacy by Enforcement）”
 * 摒弃技术噱头：在当前的区块链领域，zk-SNARKs 本身并非 $DRGX 独家特有的技术。
 * 真正的差异化在于“强制 z2z”：传统的隐私币（如 ZEC）允许用户选择透明地址（t-address），导致绝大多数交易依然暴露在外。而 $DRGX 像 Pirate Chain 一样，从协议层彻底砍掉了透明交易通道，强制要求全网只能走纯隐私地址对隐私地址（z-to-z）交易。
 * 三层隐私架构：
   * 第一层（基座）：zk-SNARKs 基础密码学；
   * 第二层（核心）：z2z-only 协议层强制隐私；

Long-term government bond yields in France, one of Europe’s established economies, have recently hit a new low. This may seem far removed from the crypto world, but in plain terms, it’s a subtle sign that global investors are reassessing risk and returns. What does this mean for crypto markets? Simply put: dollar-denominated assets are becoming less attractive, and capital may need to find somewhere new to go.

Why does this news matter?
The underlying reason is that French economic data have weakened, leading markets to think the Bank of France may need to loosen policy. More broadly, this is an early sign of a global interest-rate cycle turning downward after peaking—much like the process that followed the Fed’s last rate-hiking cycle. Other recent developments, such as U.S. Treasury yields peaking and funds flowing back into government bonds after the collapse of Silicon Valley Bank, are different facets of the same trend.

Market impact
In the short term, this could lift sentiment toward BTC and ETH, since a low-interest-rate environment tends to benefit risk assets. But the more direct impact may be on capital flows. For example, after years of aggressively buying tech stocks and Nasdaq ETFs, some investors may start shifting part of their portfolios into more stable bonds, then return to crypto when risk appetite recovers. A historical reference point: long-term bond yields did indeed remain low for an extended period after the 2008 financial crisis. Crypto was only just getting started then, but the broader trend is worth noting.

How to approach it
For now, the declining appeal of dollar-denominated assets may be a neutral-to-bullish factor for BTC, provided the Fed also begins cutting rates. If the Fed continues hiking or the European Central Bank takes a different approach, this outlook no longer holds.

What could go wrong if I copy an address directly from my transaction history when making a payment?
This is how I understand it: once an on-chain transfer is confirmed, it can't be reversed, and assets sent to a similar-looking address are basically impossible to recover.
Some token contracts allow transfers of 0 tokens. An attacker can exploit this to leave a record that looks like a transfer “from your address,” making it seem as though you sent the tokens yourself.
My current habit: before making a large transfer, I send a small test amount first, then send the rest after confirming with the recipient that it arrived.
People who frequently send and receive stablecoins and wallets with $ETH  are more likely to be targeted by address poisoning. Current price: 2058.57.

Google has open-sourced its AI computing tool Pathways on GKE, essentially giving ordinary developers supercomputing power for free. Model-training accelerators that were once only available to big tech companies can now be used by anyone working with AI. What does this mean for the cryptocurrency market? In the short term, it could boost computing-power stocks. In the long term, it could lower the barrier to AI adoption and bring more on-chain innovation to life.

The main reason behind Google's move is that the AI race has entered a highly competitive phase, and the company wants to lock in developers with its infrastructure advantage. title: 杠杆到底是啥？100U怎么撬动1000U，代价是什么
subTitle:
很多刚进场的朋友问我：10倍杠杆是不是就是赚10倍？今天用大白话讲清楚。

【本质】杠杆是交易所借钱给你开仓。你有100U本金，开10倍杠杆，实际控
制的是1000U的仓位。币价涨1%，你的本金赚10%（相对本金）；反过来，
跌1%，本金亏10%——注意，亏损是按你借来的总仓位算的。

【代价】10倍杠杆下，币价反向走约10%，你的本金就归零，这叫爆仓。不是
跌10%才亏完，是跌约10%就全部没了（准确点位还和保证金率有关）。
杠杆放大的不是你的胜率，是波动。方向对，它加速你赚钱；方向错，它加速
你出局。工具没好坏，取决于你有没有把它当工具，而不是当赌具。

【新手建议】先用2-3倍感受波动，把止损练成肌肉记忆，再谈放大。

你怎么看？评论区聊聊你的经历。

translatedData.title: What exactly is leverage? How can 100 USDT control 1,000 USDT, and what’s the cost?
translatedData.subTitle:
A lot of people who are just getting started ask me: Does 10x leverage mean you make 10 times as much? Today, I’ll explain it in plain English.

【The basics】Leverage means the exchange lends you money to open a position. If you have 100 USDT in initial capital and use 10x leverage, you actually control a position worth
1,000 USDT. If the coin price rises by 1%, you make 10% on your initial capital. In the opposite direction,
A 1% drop means a 10% loss of your initial capital—note that the loss is calculated based on your total borrowed position.

【The cost】With 10x leverage, if the coin price moves against you by about 10%, your initial capital is wiped out. This is called liquidation. It’s not
that you only lose everything after a 10% drop—you can lose it all after a drop of about 10% (the exact threshold also depends on the margin ratio).

First, what is address poisoning, and why does it fool people?
Checking only the first and last few characters of an address won’t protect you from address poisoning, because it’s not hard to generate an address with the same beginning and ending.
Address poisoning is when scammers generate a lookalike address with the same beginning and ending as an address you commonly use, then slip it into your transaction history.
Before making a payment, check the entire address. Don’t just check the beginning and end—make sure the middle characters match too.
Wallets that frequently transfer stablecoins, as well as the wallet at $ETH , are more likely to be targeted by address poisoning.

Starting November 26, private customers of Israel’s Discount Bank will be able to buy and sell Bitcoin and Ethereum in their bank’s app. The proceeds from sales will go into their bank account, but for now, the crypto can’t be transferred out.

On November 11, the bank announced on its website and in a press release that this is the first time in Israeli banking that customers can directly buy, sell, and hold Bitcoin and Ethereum in a banking app. Transactions will use customers’ existing securities accounts, so there’s no need to open an account with an overseas exchange or manage private keys themselves. The bank also stated that for now, this is a “closed system”: purchased crypto cannot be transferred to an external institution or to the customer’s own on-chain address, and crypto from outside cannot be transferred in. Whether transfers will be enabled in the future depends on regulatory and business developments.

Here are the key points that matter to everyday users 👇

🔹 Who can use it: The service is available only to private customers aged 18 or over who are in Israel and already have a securities account. They must first sign the relevant securities and complex-products terms, then complete a separate agreement in the app before placing an order. Corporate accounts are not eligible this time.

🔹 How trading works: In the app, go to “All actions → Capital markets → Digital currency trading.” For now, only immediate trades are available; future limit orders cannot be placed. Bitcoin and Ethereum can both be purchased in increments starting at 0.01 units. Trading hours are Sunday to Friday, 9:00–23:00 Israel time, in line with the bank’s trading room hours.

🔹 Fees and settlement: The trading fee is 2% of the transaction amount, with an additional foreign-exchange fee if currency conversion is required. Custody fees will be waived for six months from the launch on November 26, then charged quarterly at 0.25%. The crypto will appear in the securities portfolio immediately, while funds will be credited or debited on the next business day (T+1). Sale proceeds will be credited in U.S. dollars; customers must instruct the bank themselves if they want to convert them to shekels.

🔹 Tax: The bank says capital gains and losses on digital currencies can be offset against capital gains and losses on other securities in the same account. The tax rate on profits is 25%, and tax is handled at the bank before the funds are paid out. The bank emphasizes that this offset applies only to capital gains.

The bank also cautions that digital currencies are not legal tender and do not have the same protections as securities. They are highly volatile, and customers could lose their entire principal. Several Israeli media outlets report that the wallet infrastructure is provided by Fireblocks; the website describes the service and custody as being handled by an “authorized third party.”

This isn’t a button you can click just yet. You’ll have to wait until November 26 and sign the agreement before trading is actually enabled in the app.

content:
11月26日起，以色列Discount Bank的私人客户可以在自家银行 App 里买卖比特币和以太坊——卖出的钱会进银行账户，币却暂时出不去。

银行 11 月 11 日在官网和新闻稿里宣布：这是以色列银行业第一次在银行 App 里直接做比特币、以太坊的买卖和持有。交易走的是客户已有的证券账户，不用再去开境外交易所账户，也不用自己管私钥。银行自己也写明了，眼下这是一套「封闭系统」：买来的币不能转到外部机构或自己的链上地址，外面的币也转不进来；以后会不会开放，要看监管和业务进展。

对普通人真正有影响的几条是这些 👇

🔹 谁能用：只对年满 18 岁、人在以色列、已经开通证券账户的私人客户开放。要先签好证券和复杂产品相关条款，再在 App 里完成专门协议，才能下单。公司账户这次用不了。

🔹 交易怎么走：App 里「全部操作 → 资本市场 → 数字货币交易」，目前只有即时成交，不能挂未来的限价单。比特币和以太坊都可以按 0.01 个单位起买。交易时间是周日到周五 9:00–23:00（以色列时间），跟银行交易室营业时间对齐。

🔹 费用和到账：买卖手续费按成交额的 2% 收，如需换汇还要另算汇兑费。托管费从 11 月 26 日上线起免半年，之后按季度收 0.25%。币会马上出现在证券组合里，资金则是下一个工作日（T+1）入账或扣款。卖掉后进账的是美元，要不要换成谢克尔，得客户自己下指令。

🔹 税务：官方说，数字货币的资本盈亏可以和同一账户里其他证券的资本盈亏互相抵扣，利润税率为 25%，而且是在银行端做税前处理。它特别强调，这种抵扣只针对资本利得。

银行还提醒：数字货币不是法币，也不享受和证券一样的保障，波动大，存在本金全部亏掉的可能。多家以色列媒体写到，钱包基础设施由 Fireblocks 提供；官网措辞是「经授权的第三方」负责服务和托管。

这不是已经能点的按钮。要等到 11 月 26 日，并且把协议签完，App 里才会真正放开下单。

📰 Why has Ondo’s RWA market soared to $4 billion? What makes the tokenized asset ecosystem so appealing to institutions?

Ondo Finance announced that the total value of its tokenized real-world asset products has surpassed $4 billion, covering 484 different assets and more than 560,000 holders. Institutional-grade RWA markets have reached this scale for the first time—exceeding the combined total of all comparable products to date.

Why does this news matter?
The core reason is that RWA solves the liquidity challenges of bringing traditional assets on-chain. Through tokenization, Ondo breaks down assets such as office buildings and infrastructure—which can’t be bought and sold directly—into smaller, divisible, tradable units, much like shares. Institutions can hold these assets without posting collateral, while regulators can track funds through the blockchain. The RWA market was previously small because only a handful of players dared to enter. Now Ondo has lowered the barriers, which means institutional allocation to these alternative assets could become a self-reinforcing cycle.

Market impact
This is positive for short-term sentiment around BTC and ETH. As a foundational DeFi infrastructure layer, BTC could see its network value rise as institutional capital flows into RWA. ETH’s Layer 2 ecosystem could benefit from demand for RWA use cases, especially as high-performance solutions such as ZK-RWA are rolled out faster. In the long term, RWA could draw huge pools of existing capital from traditional finance into Web3, reshaping the market landscape. As the boom in REIT ETFs after the 2008 financial crisis illustrates, the rise of RWA represents a genuine paradigm shift in financial technology.

Trading approach
This news has greater implications for ETH. If ETH opens up more on-chain interfaces for RWA interactions in the future, it could potentially bring some holders who are sitting on losses back into action in the short term. However, keep in mind that tokenizing claims to RWA yields is still at an early stage. It’s important to monitor the actual collateralization ratios of the underlying assets, as well as whether yield distribution complies with regulations. If there’s a risk of capital outflows, this thesis no longer holds.

Ondo Finance宣布其代币化现实世界资产产品总价值突破40亿美元，涵盖484个不同资产，持有者超56万。这是机构级RWA市场深度首次达到这个量级，比之前所有同类产品总和还要多。

为什么这条新闻重要？
这事儿根本原因在于RWA解决了传统资产上链的流动性难题。Ondo用代币化把写字楼、基础设施这类不能直接买卖的资产，拆分成可拆分、可交易的小份，就像股票一样。机构能不用押品就能持有这类资产，监管机构也能通过区块链追踪资金。之前RWA市场规模小是因为只有少数玩家敢做，现在Ondo把门槛降下来了，意味着机构配置这类另类资产的逻辑会形成正循环。

对市场的影响
这对BTC和ETH的短期情绪是正面的。BTC作为DeFi基础设施层，RWA机构资金流入会抬高其网络价值；ETH的Layer2生态受益于RWA场景需求，特别是ZK-RWA这类高性能方案会加速落地。长期看，RWA把传统金融的巨额存量资金虹吸到Web3，会重塑市场格局。参考2008年金融危机后REITsETF爆发的案例，这次RWA的崛起是金融科技真正的范式转移。

操作思路
这条消息对ETH的意义更大。如果ETH未来能开放更多RWA链上交互接口，预计短期内会激活部分套牢盘。但要注意，目前RWA的收益权代币化仍处于早期，需要关注底层资产的真实抵押率，以及监管对收益分配方式的合规性。如果出现资金抽离风险，这个逻辑就作废了。

subTitle:
本金几百上千U的朋友最焦虑：这么点钱怎么翻身？先说结论：小资金的
优势恰恰是「船小好调头」，别拿大资金的打法硬套。

【三个建议】1. 合约杠杆别超过5倍，小本金最大的敌人是归零，不是
赚得慢；2. 把80%精力从「找百倍币」挪到「练执行」——同样是练手，
拿小仓位在BTC/ETH上练，比在小币上练生存率高得多（至少不容易
被一根针带走）；3. 每月有结余就补点本金，本金曲线平滑上升，比

📰 Why Is Testing Ethereum Upgrades So Difficult? Sprinter Co-Founder Reveals All

Ethereum upgrade tests keep running into problems—even code that has just made it onto the testnet can’t get working properly. A Sprinter co-founder says it’s because Ethereum is so complex and the risks are so high that no one dares make changes lightly. It’s a big deal for the crypto world, since every upgrade could trigger sharp price swings in Bitcoin and Ethereum.

Why does this news matter?
Difficult upgrade testing means every major release could run into trouble. For example, last year’s testing of the Merge to Layer 2 had bugs pop up again and again, directly slowing down the upgrade process. Sprinter says the key issue is Ethereum’s complexity: cross-chain systems, smart contracts, Layer 2... it’s all piled together, and changing one part could affect every feature. It’s like rewiring a skyscraper—you wouldn’t start work without testing everything inside out.

Market impact
In the short term, news that testing is difficult may make Ethereum bulls hesitate, because every failed test makes the market question whether the upgrade will fail. In the long run, however, this caution may actually be a good thing, helping avoid disasters like the sudden collapse of Solana’s testnet. More importantly, difficult testing could make the Ethereum team more likely to upgrade in stages—for example, upgrading a particular Layer 2 first, then changing the mainnet once things are stable. This strategy may slow innovation, but it prioritizes reliability.

In a nutshell: Testing Ethereum upgrades is like walking a tightrope—one misstep could send you falling, but taking the long way around wastes time.

Trading outlook
Ethereum’s testing challenges are neutral for ETH’s price, but could boost BTC’s safe-haven appeal. If bugs continue to emerge during testing, the ETH/BTC exchange rate could edge down from its current 1:36 to 1:38. But be cautious: if testing is suddenly canceled, ETH could drop straight to $1,980. If XRP suddenly surges past $1.15, this thesis no longer holds.

Although it’s still unclear how serious the specific threat is, the uncertainty has already left investors on edge.
